title: Partner inference onboarding: data handling manifest & attestation (template)
summary: A compact onboarding manifest for partners integrating managed inference or private deployment connections. Combines a minimal DPA-style data handling checklist, required technical controls, and an attestation statement the partner signs during onboarding. Intended for early-stage integrations where full contract annexes are negotiated later.
body:
Purpose:
This template is intended to accelerate safe partner onboarding for inference integrations (hosted API clients, dedicated capacity customers, or private connectors). It captures required data handling commitments, minimum technical controls, evidence items, and a short attestation the partner signs. Use as a precursor to formal contract annexes (DPA, Security Addendum).

Scope:
Applies to third parties ("partners") that will send inference queries or otherwise access Redwood-managed inference endpoints. Covers classification of data types, permitted use, logging and telemetry, retention, and incident obligations. Not a substitute for a full DPA for regulated customers.

Definitions (short):
- "Sensitive Query": any input or output that includes personal data, credentials, or PII as defined by applicable law.
- "Ephemeral KV/Cache": runtime key-value or prompt caches used to accelerate recurrent inference.
- "Evidence Artifact": logs, screenshots, or exportable records used to verify a control.

Minimum required commitments (partner):
1) Data minimization: Only send fields necessary for the inference task. Avoid embedding full records or unredacted PII unless explicitly authorized.
2) Allowed data flows: Partner must specify the data centers/regions from/to which queries will originate. Cross-border transfers require prior notice.
3) Retention: Query inputs and full outputs must be retained no longer than 30 days by default; if the partner requires longer retention, they must justify and agree to additional safeguards.
4) Ephemeral caching: Partner acknowledges and accepts that runtime caches may persist KV/prefix data for performance. If the partner requires non-caching, they must use the no-cache flag or dedicated routing and document that requirement.
5) Logging & telemetry: Redwood will collect telemetry for operational reasons (latency, errors, token counts). Partners may not reconfigure Redwood telemetry; partners must supply their own telemetry if they need additional instrumentation.

Technical controls (minimum):
- TLS 1.2+ for all endpoints; mutual TLS required for private connectors.
- API authentication with rotating credentials; support for short-lived tokens (<= 24 hours) for critical systems.
- Per-tenant encryption-at-rest for stored artifacts; partner must designate whether data is encrypted by customer-managed keys.
- Access controls: least privilege for service accounts. Document all accounts with access to partner data.
- Query scrubbers: partners must provide a short plan for automatic redaction of known secrets and PII patterns in requests where applicable.

Operational controls & evidence (what Redwood asks for during onboarding):
- Network diagram: IP ranges, NATs, and carrier hops (screenshot or document).
- List of privileged roles and names (or role descriptions) that can access partner data.
- Evidence of vulnerability scanning cadence (weekly/quarterly) and patch policy.
- Retention policy excerpt showing the 30-day default for query logs.
- Pen-test summary or SOC/ISO attestation if available (redacted OK).

Incident response & notification:
- Partners must notify Redwood within 24 hours of discovering a confirmed data exposure affecting Redwood-managed inference traffic or artifacts.
- Notification must include: scope, root cause (if known), mitigation actions taken, and planned remediation timeline.
- Redwood will coordinate escalation with the partner and reserves the right to suspend queries to mitigate active exfiltration.

Audit & sampling rights:
- Redwood may request sampling evidence to validate controls during onboarding. For production customers, a limited remote audit (or evidence folder) is required annually.
- Evidence examples: export of role membership, logs demonstrating retention deletion, and screenshots of configuration pages.

Minimal contractual clauses (to include in initial SOW or MSA amendment):
- Limited Purpose: Partner agrees to use inference outputs solely for the agreed feature set and not to retrain models with Redwood-provided endpoints unless explicitly permitted.
- Data handling: Partner agrees to the retention and deletion windows in this manifest; deviations require written approval.
- Indemnity carveout: Partner must indemnify Redwood for breaches caused by negligent exposure of partner data.
- Escalation & termination: Redwood may suspend service for security reasons with notice and will provide remediation guidance.

Attestation (sign-off block for partner):
By signing below, the authorized representative of the partner confirms that the partner: (a) has read and will comply with the commitments above; (b) will provide requested evidence during onboarding; and (c) acknowledges Redwood's right to suspend traffic in the event of an immediate security risk.

Partner legal name: ____________________
Authorized signer: ____________________
Title: ____________________
Date: ____________________

Onboarding timeline (recommended):
- Day 0: Intake form + network ranges supplied.
- Day 1–3: Technical contact verification, initial evidence delivery (network diagram, roles).
- Day 4–7: Test integration in staging with no-cache flag enabled for sensitive datasets.
- Day 8–14: Evidence validation and final attestation.

Notes & negotiation placeholders (for internal use):
- If partner requests >30 day retention, add a retention exhibit with specific encryption and access controls.
- For private deployments with customer-managed KMS, require key rotation evidence and KMS access policy export.
- For high-risk regulated partners, escalate to legal for a full DPA and SOC2/SOC3 evidence.

Document history & next steps:
- Drafted by: Maya Alvarez (security-and-compliance).
- Reviewers: Ethan Park (infra), Sana Iqbal (privacy), Liam O'Connor (solutions eng).
- Next: Run one pilot onboarding using this manifest and capture missing evidence items to refine the template.

End of template.
